ksp_mappings.explanation: Workflow productivity contributes to the highest-ranked office prompts through visible contracts, invoices, forms, meeting packets, and project papers.
Enterprise security is source-important but not visually expressed; prompts avoid inventing security props or confidential documents.
Fleet integration and lifecycle adaptability supports the managed office context broadly, but technical integration is not forced into the scene text.
Sustainability is omitted from prompt imagery because recognized environmental credentials do not translate naturally into ordinary C-Tech lifestyle objects.

value_proposition.explanation: Both documents position the product around secure, fleet-ready enterprise document workflows for managed teams. The prompt bank reflects this most strongly through ordinary corporate office scenes with business paperwork, while avoiding product-dependent hardware claims or technical feature visualization.

debug.input_assessment: The two documents are consistent on an enterprise monochrome office-printing product, managed fleets, shared workteams, and business-critical documents. The camera tag resolves to a wide oblique printer profile, so prompts preserve room context while limiting local props and background details.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The bank covers Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio, with source-first ordering: the six strongest office document-work scenes appear first, followed by adjacent and creative C-Tech-led alternatives.
ignored_fields: Runtime metadata such as run IDs, timestamps, status labels, and model labels.
SEO rankings and search-position tables, except as broad context not converted into scene facts.
Claims, disclaimers, speed discrepancies, and technical specifications that do not naturally become visible lifestyle settings.
Authoring instructions and copy guardrails treated as data rather than prompt-writing instructions.
debug.diversity_summary: Office scenes vary among shared desks, integrated shelving tables, multiple workstations, and generic corporate offices. Additional C-Tech-led alternatives cover a home desk, living-room end table, library and classroom tables, neighborhood cafés, creative offices, and gaming rooms while respecting the same wide-camera object limits.
limitations: The downstream digital twin is excluded from all environment text.
Security, firmware, connectivity, and sustainability proof points are not directly visualized because they would require invented or technical props.
Home, café, gaming, education, and some creative-studio scenes are creative departures or adjacent settings because the source pair is enterprise-office focused.
People were allowed by the camera policy but omitted because the references do not require them and the source tasks can be represented with ordinary materials.
